name: mscse-dual-degree-shared-nine
description: Academic Code §2.2 (“No more than nine credit hours of classes from any one master’s degree may be counted toward any other graduate degree”) and DGS Handbook §2.9 — policy review 2026-10-04, P2-ac-1-3-2 (and P2-dh-front-1-2-7 case b); DGS: “Apply suggested handling”. An MSCSE student enrolled in a second Notre Dame master’s at the same time, with the dual plan of study approved, ticks four CSE courses (12 credits) as also counting toward the other degree: nine of them count toward the MSCSE and the fourth is refused as beyond the allowance — instead of all twelve. The Fall 2025 semester, every course of it shared, is still a full-time registration (Academic Code §3.5).

detailIncludes: 9 of the 9 credits shared with your other degree used
CSE 60427: 3 credits not counted — beyond the allowance
